gemini-2.5-flash.standardized_narrative: In 2017, Syndicate 2001 experienced an aggregate gross prior year reserve strengthening of GBP 71.5 million. This was primarily driven by a large number of catastrophe losses and tough market conditions impacting attritional claims experience, leading to strengthening of prior years' reserves in Property and Casualty. This was partly offset by GBP 22 million of prior period reserve releases in Reinsurance, reflecting a net improvement to previously booked large losses. Significant catastrophe events like Hurricanes Harvey, Irma and Maria, the Mexican earthquake, and California wildfires contributed to the overall claims deterioration.

Management reported a net prior period release of GBP 22.0m driven by improvements on previously booked large losses. However, 2017 underwriting was materially impacted by significant catastrophe activity (notably Hurricanes Harvey, Irma and Maria, the Mexican earthquake and the California wildfires) and a high volume of larger losses which worsened the current year claims experience. The net prior year movement reported in the narrative is a modest release (~1.1% of opening gross reserves) driven by favourable development on large prior claims.
